links.outcome: Sensitivity-specificity tradeoffs and threshold variation across LLMs in identifying missed diagnoses
links.effect: Similar discrimination but different binary thresholds; 72-hour cohort sensitivity 42.9% (GPT-5 mini) to 85.7% (Claude Sonnet 4); specificity 55.9% to 82.9%.
links.quote: Across cohorts, LLMs showed similar discrimination but different sensitivity-specificity tradeoffs; Claude Sonnet 4 generally favored higher sensitivity, whereas GPT-5 mini favored higher specificity.

links.outcome: LLM performance variation across cohorts on local retrospective health-system data
links.effect: Floor-to-ICU cohort sensitivity ranged from 5.6% (GPT-5 mini) to 55.6% (Claude Sonnet 4); AUC 0.57 to 0.82; performance varied by cohort.
links.quote: In this diagnostic study of 2 ED eTrigger cohorts, model performance varied by cohort, with LLMs showing similar discrimination but different binary thresholds.

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs to screen eTrigger-flagged ED encounters for missed opportunities in diagnosis

screen.reason: Retrospective study evaluating LLMs (Claude, GPT, Gemini) for identifying missed opportunities for diagnosis (MODs) in ED eTrigger cohorts compared to physician review; does not evaluate a specific implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
